clause_i.reason: For D=proxy_buttons, the generator samples different initial states from the exact depth-14 frontier, so histories with the same prior-action history can require different next disc/direction choices. A policy using only I_t therefore cannot be optimal across all such states.

clause_ii.reason: The current and reference rose arrangements and the six visible controls are present in one screenshot. A bounded zero-duration window is sufficient to choose a state-dependent turn; consecutive frames are not needed.

clause_iii.reason: There is no autonomous transition during any positive wait. The browser model is initialized once, and current state changes only when attempt() handles a turn input; refused turns leave the visible state unchanged. With no H_t to H_t^tau task-state evolution, no available turn becomes unavailable or strictly less effective inside a delay.

common_visible_process: None. The rose is static while the agent supplies no new action; legal turns synchronously change the state only after a button click. The visible reference/current arrangement is useful for static planning but is not a changing process, so clauses (i) and (ii) cannot be combined with clause (iii).

pre_run.reason: The mathematical definition already fails at clause (iii), so the pre-run override is not needed. No autonomous outcome phase exists in this configuration.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 5 uses scramble_depth 14; simplified mode is implemented as six labelled clockwise/counter-clockwise proxy buttons, and the configured observation window is 0 ms with one frame.
The environment is synchronous and configured with observation_window_ms 0 and frames_per_observation 1; no task-time mechanic is declared.
legal() and turn() are pure state operations; generation samples a depth-14 initial permutation and emits a static rose contract plus a solution path, with no clock, timer, or autonomous update.

Simplified rendering creates the six proxy buttons, their click handlers call attempt(), and current is updated only by that input handler; rendering initializes the model from initial_state and contains no autonomous task-state loop.
The mechanic stylesheet contains presentation rules only and no keyframe or timed animation that changes the rose state.
The grader binds simplified input to proxy_buttons and grades by replaying legal/turn events to the solved state; it uses no task-time evolution.
The exported verifier independently replays the submitted event transcript and final state, with no time-dependent or autonomous-state check.
The solver's simplified path is a sequence of visible button clicks followed by successful-turn checks; it does not require timed waiting or observation of a moving state.
